findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass the account password
findings.body: The password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is nonempty (line 121), but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and does not validate that TOTP value at all. A request to the credentials callback containing an email, any arbitrary nonempty `totpCode`, and a valid `backupCode` therefore authenticates without the password. Backup codes are presented by the UI as a replacement for the authenticator after the primary login, not as passwordless credentials; this permits anyone with a copied/stolen backup code to sign in directly. Verify the primary credential independently of the selected second-factor method, or use a server-side first-factor challenge state before accepting either TOTP or a backup code.

findings.title: Backup codes are not consumed atomically
findings.body: The code is validated from a previously read `user.backupCodes` value and then consumed with an unconditional `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both decrypt and find the code before either update completes; both requests then succeed and write an equivalent array with that entry set to null. This violates the advertised single-use guarantee and can yield multiple authenticated sessions from one recovery code. Consume the code with an atomic compare-and-set/transactional update that predicates on the current encrypted value (or store individual hashed codes with a unique/conditional consumed state), and reject the request when that update affects no row.
